analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation, at docs/reference/configuration.md line 410 (head). The DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK row now lists ClusterServiceCommand.swift (supervisorConfiguration) as a reader and says the variable skips the `darkbloom cluster` pair's update at its slot. No code, protocol, key-custody or authorization behaviour changes in the supplied evidence.

Security relevance: DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK is an operator-controlled environment variable that disables auto-update. The operator can already do this, so it adds no capability for ADV-001. It touches the update and rollback surface (T-013, T-043) only as documentation. The variable is an existing, documented opt-out, and the row records that the cluster supervisor now honours it. It does not alter attestation, the binary-hash registry (A-011) or the App Attest authorization boundary (TB-011).

The rest of the file was reviewed as unchanged context. It is consistent with the existing threat model: the worker qualification flags are default-off and use exact `1`. The add-on socket and sandbox root variables are not forwarded to launchd. The sandbox installer must use https and is capped at 1 MiB (T-061). Prefix-cache defaults match T-041 (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kill switch). No secrets appear.

Unverified contract: I cannot see ClusterServiceCommand.swift, so I could not confirm that the cluster supervisor really reads this variable. An update skip there would still be operator-controlled and fail-safe in the sense that it only prevents updates. Cluster mode (ClusterLocalCommand, GLM qualification) is outside the supplied source units, so its trust boundary was not examined. No finding is raised.
